quotes.text:
The fact that the .status.loadBalancer field can be set while .spec.type
is not "LoadBalancer" is a flub.  Any spec update will already clear
.status.ingress, so it's hard to really rely on this.  After this
change, updates which try to set this combination will fail validation.
quotes.author: Tim Hockin
quotes.title: Gate: disallow .status.loadBalancer on non-LB svc

quotes.text:
Changelog suggestion
```diff
-Setting the `status.loadBalancer` of a Service whose `spec.type` is not "LoadBalancer" was previously allowed, but any update to the `metadata` or `spec` would wipe that field.  Setting this field is no longer permitted unless `spec.type` is  "LoadBalancer".  In the very unlikely event that this has unexpected impact, the "AllowServiceLBStatusOnNonLB" feature gate may be set to true, which will restore the previous behavior.
quotes.author: sftim
quotes.title: PR #119789

medium: The passages detail a restriction preventing the setting of `status.loadBalancer` when `spec.type` is not 'LoadBalancer', due to potential data inconsistencies and validation failures.

card.what: This line prevents setting the `status.loadBalancer` field on a service if the service type is not a Load Balancer and the `status.Ingress` field is not empty.
card.why: Tim Hockin initially identified a problem where setting the `status.loadBalancer` field on non-Load Balancer services was allowed, but updates would immediately clear the field [1][2]. He reasoned that relying on this behavior was fragile due to the way updates cleared the `status.ingress` field. The change was intended to enforce that this combination of fields should not be set, preventing validation failures [2][3].
card.next: Check if there are any downstream systems or processes that depend on this validation logic, and assess the potential impact of removing it.

answer: A deprecated feature gate must first be locked to its default for some releases before it can be removed; removing it early broke emulated versions.
